name: Keycloak introspection client (RFC 7662)
purpose: The verifier the mechanism uses when the realm record's `verificationMode` is `introspection`. Owns the RFC 7662 request shape (HTTP basic auth with `clientId:clientSecret`, `token` form parameter), the response handling, the optional short-lived cache, and the extraction of the verified claim record the role adapter reads.
responsibilities: Issue a POST to the record's `introspection_endpoint` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `Authorization: Basic <base64(clientId:clientSecret)>`, and body `token=<the-access-token>` (AC-11105-1).

Parse the response body as JSON per RFC 7662; a response with `active: true` yields the claim record; a response with `active: false` refuses the token with `KEYCLOAK_INTROSPECTION_INACTIVE` (AC-11105-2).
Refuse a non-2xx response with `KEYCLOAK_INTROSPECTION_ENDPOINT_ERROR` naming the HTTP status class; emit `keycloak.introspection_refused` carrying realmSlug and status class (AC-11105-3).

Cache the response when the record's `introspectionCacheTtlSeconds` is greater than zero; cache key is a stable hash of the token value (SHA-256 hex prefix, never the token) so the cache does not carry token strings; default TTL is 0 (no cache); AC-11105-1 covers the uncached path.
Emit one structured audit event `keycloak.introspection_verified` on a 2xx `active: true` carrying realmSlug and no token value (AC-11105-1).
internalStructure: One factory function producing an introspect closure over the discovery client (for the endpoint), an injected `httpFetch`, an injected clock, and an injected auditSink. The optional cache is a Map keyed by the token-hash whose value is `{ claims, cachedAt }`; entries evict on TTL expiry from the read path.

interfaces.name: auditSink
interfaces.description: Structured-event sink; never invoked with a token value.

dependencies.name: Discovery client
dependencies.description: Provides the introspection endpoint from discovery.

tradeoffs: The introspection round-trip is expensive on the hot path; the optional cache lets an operator on a high-issuance realm claw back some of the cost at the price of a bounded revocation-reflection delay. Hashing the token as the cache key defends against a leaked cache dump: nothing on disk (or in a warmed memory dump) is a token; the hash cannot be exchanged. Refusing on non-2xx keeps the mechanism from falling back to a permissive posture when the endpoint is misbehaving.
